answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by charging a small refundable stake locked while an identity is active, like a terrace built on basalt: cheap to stand on once, expensive to fake a thousand times. New identities start inside a nebula of untrusted peers, earning trust only through attested work that costs real time and compute. An attacker cloning identities must pay the stake and the work cost for every copy, while honest agents pay once and keep their reputation, so forgery scales linearly in cost while honest participation stays cheap.
